shared_conventions.screen_direction_basis: Screen sides are taken from what composition.json / blocking.json already computed off each scene's layout.json orientation (top_of_map + landmark xy), NOT re-derived from compass bearings here. This station checks RELATIONAL consistency: whether a named pair (figure/figure, figure/landmark, figure/prop) keeps the same left-right order across a cut, and whether a travel or eyeline direction reverses. A shot on the travel axis (head-on or straight-away) is treated as neutral and licenses a side change after it, per standard 180-degree practice.
shared_conventions.axis_scope: Every one of the 100 cuts in the episode was checked, inside groups and across group boundaries, within scenes. Cuts between scenes are listed but a scene change is not by itself an axis violation.
shared_conventions.time_of_day: Every group in ep01 is early_afternoon. Waking clock ~14:00-15:05 GMT, Friday 4 July 1862; S03-S10 are dream scenes inside that same slot (cinematography.json color_temp.self_consistency_note). There is no day/night jump anywhere in the episode. The one non-monotonic clock step is grp001 -> grp002, and it is the declared flash-forward FF-ep01-open (TR-01 in / TR-02 out), not a continuity error.
shared_conventions.costume_basis: Outfits are inherited verbatim from shot_list.json (group costumes_by_char / per-shot costumes), not re-decided here. bible/costumes.json change_point_summary lists no change point earlier than ev0018, so no ep01 shot is anywhere near a change point and no group boundary is forced by wardrobe. This station's increment is the per-shot state phrase, written as a short English phrase for 08-video-gen/prompt to append verbatim after the costume visual_en.
shared_conventions.state_monotonicity: Damage, soiling and wetness only ever increase or are removed by a staged cause on screen. In ep01 there is exactly one legitimate removal: the dry earth dust is not brushed off, it is simply overtaken by water from sh071 onward. Nothing in this episode heals or dries.
shared_conventions.injuries: There are none anywhere in ep01. Screenplay S04: 'She is not a bit hurt.' No shot may show a graze, bruise, torn cloth or blood on any character.
shared_conventions.entity_separation: CRE-001 'Wild White Rabbit' (creature, real, mute, unclothed, pink-eyed, true rabbit scale) appears ONLY in sh008, sh010, sh012 (grp004, grp006) and is offscreen-present in sh007 and sh011. CHAR-white-rabbit 'White Rabbit' (character, COS-006 checked silk waistcoat, speaks) appears ONLY in sh027-sh029, sh031 (grp011, grp012) and sh073, sh074, sh076, sh077 (grp028, grp029). They are never the same entity, never share a shot, and never share a reference image.
shared_conventions.long_take: OFF for this project (settings duration.long_take = false; shot_list.json long_take field says the same). Consequence enforced below: every one of the 36 group_transitions carries anchor 'none'. No group takes a tail frame or a tail-segment continuation from the group before it, and no continuity_ref is created anywhere.
shared_conventions.continuity_ref_audit: Searched the whole project tree for 'continuity_ref' and 'video_refs': zero hits. No pre-existing continuity_ref link exists to report or to build on. shot_list.json generation_groups[].continuity_from IS populated (each group points at its predecessor) but it is an ORDERING pointer required by the host check code/check_generation_groups.py and must not be read as a tail-frame anchor - shot_list.json states this in its own long_take field, and the host preview reads the anchor from THIS file's group_transitions[].anchor, not from continuity_from.
shared_conventions.carrier_of_continuity: With anchor 'none' everywhere, continuity across every cut is carried by WRITTEN continuity only. Each group_transitions entry therefore states, in words, what must match across the join: wardrobe and its state, prop position and which hand or mouth holds it, body position and posture, light source and direction, and time of day.

axis_violations.finding: The camera crosses the Alice / Sister line. sh002 is the meadow-side wide (composition: 'the meadow-side camera puts south on the left') with Alice screen-left at 0.44 and the Sister screen-right at 0.54. sh003 is the water-side medium-close, which puts Alice screen-right at 0.66 with the Sister's forearm crossing screen-left. The water-side axis established by sh003 then holds unbroken for the rest of the scene (sh005 Alice 0.62 / Sister 0.33, sh009 Alice 0.63 / Sister 0.33), so the episode crosses the line once, at the move from the establishing wide into the scene's working axis, and never again.

axis_violations.finding: The rabbit's exit direction is contradicted by the shot that reacts to it. In sh008 CRE-001 enters 'from the open meadow on screen-right', crosses right-to-left across the near ground and goes away into depth toward the way across the field (layout field_way [0.90, 0.22], i.e. left of and beyond the lens axis). sh009 is the water-side axis of sh005, where north is screen-left (the Sister sits at 0.33) and therefore screen-right is the opposite side of the field from where the rabbit went; but sh009's composition gaze reads 'she stares after the rabbit out of the LOWER RIGHT of frame' and blocking sh009 facing reads 'first out to screen-right after the animal'. Cutting from an animal leaving screen-left-and-away to a girl looking screen-right after him reads as her looking at something else.
axis_violations.routed_to: 07-directing/composition (sh009 composition.json gaze) and 07-directing/blocking (sh009 blocking.json facing) - both files carry the same wrong side and must be changed together.

Two fixes are available and the choice is composition's, not mine: (a) turn sh009's look to screen-left-and-into-depth, which costs nothing but puts the look after the rabbit on the same side as the look up to the Sister; or (b) leave sh009 and re-point sh008's exit so the animal leaves screen-right-and-away, which is a one-line change to sh008 but must not disturb sh008's 'right to left across the near ground' pass over her shoes, which is the shot's whole point.
